facts.statement: Infernodrakon is a genus of azhdarchid pterosaurs from the Upper Cretaceous Hell Creek Formation in Montana, United States.
facts.quote: Infernodrakon (meaning "dragon from hell") is a genus of azhdarchid pterosaurs from the Upper Cretaceous Hell Creek Formation of Montana, United States.

facts.statement: The genus Infernodrakon contains only one species, I. hastacollis, which is known from a single neck vertebra.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, I. hastacollis, known from a single neck vertebra.

facts.statement: Based on comparisons with related azhdarchids, Infernodrakon probably had a wingspan of about 4.15 meters.
facts.quote: Based on comparisons with related azhdarchids, it probably had a wingspan of about 4.15 m.

facts.statement: In 2002, the holotype specimen BMR P2002.2, a fifth cervical vertebra of an azhdarchid pterosaur, was found alongside a tyrannosauroid specimen in the Maastrichtian-age Hell Creek Formation in Carter County, Montana.
facts.quote: In 2002, a tyrannosauroid specimen (BMR P2002.4.1, "Jane", now the holotype of Nanotyrannus lethaeus) was recovered from strata belonging to the Maastrichtian-age Hell Creek Formation in Carter County, Montana, United States. Alongside that specimen was the fifth cervical (neck) vertebra of an azhdarchid pterosaur. Catalogued as BMR P2002.2, it was originally assigned to cf. Quetzalcoatlus sp.

facts.statement: In 2025, a team led by Emily Thomas, David W. E. Hone, Timothy Gomes, and Joseph E. Peterson re-examined the specimen and determined it belonged to a new genus more closely related to Arambourgiania philadelphiae than to Quetzalcoatlus.
facts.quote: In 2025, a team consisting of Emily Thomas, David W. E. Hone, Timothy Gomes, and Joseph E. Peterson re-examined the specimen, determining that it belonged to a novel genus more closely related to Arambourgiania philadelphiae from Jordan than to Quetzalcoatlus.

facts.statement: The preserved neck vertebra is extremely elongated and gracile, with an elongation ratio of 15.1.
facts.quote: This bone is extremely elongated and gracile; the ratio of the preserved length to the width at the middle of the centrum ('elongation ratio') is 15.1.

facts.statement: More recent analyses suggest that azhdarchids hunted small terrestrial prey in a model known as the 'terrestrial stalking' hypothesis.
facts.quote: Though azhdarchid lifestyles have long been debated, more recent analyses suggest that they hunted small terrestrial prey. This model is known as the 'terrestrial stalking' hypothesis.

facts.statement: Infernodrakon belongs to the family Azhdarchidae.
The type species of the genus Infernodrakon is Infernodrakon hastacollis.
Infernodrakon lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Due to its medium size and slender neck vertebrae, Infernodrakon was likely poorly adapted for handling large prey.
facts.quote: Infernodrakon, siendo un azdárquido de tamaño mediano con vértebras del cuello gráciles, probablemente habría estado mal adaptado para el estrés de sujetar o engullir animales grandes.

facts.statement: Infernodrakon is identified as a mesopredator that likely consumed small animals such as juvenile archosaurs, lizards, snakes, mammals, amphibians, and eggs.
facts.quote: Como tal, puede ser identificado como un mesopredador, probablemente consumiendo pequeños animales incluyendo arcosaurios juveniles, escamosos (lagartos y serpientes), mamíferos, anfibios y huevos.

facts.statement: While the lifestyle of azhdarchids has long been debated, recent analyses suggest they hunted small terrestrial prey.
facts.quote: Aunque se ha debatido hace tiempo el estilo de vida de los azdárquidos, los análisis más recientes sugieren que cazaban pequeñas presas terrestres.
